answer: To keep cheap clones from flooding the market, an agent economy can require every new identity to tend a bonded work garden: a public plot of tasks whose outputs peers can re-run. Admission samples a random plume of those artifacts and demands the claimant regenerate their hashes under a short deadline. Failures drop into a cooling lagoon, a time-locked pool where stake stays frozen until more unique work accrues, so copying identities costs more than contributing honestly.
